newsitem.title: USA: CalPERS recruits fund managers via the Internet.
newsitem.headline: CalPERS recruits fund managers via the Internet.

text.p: The California Public Employees' Retirement System (CalPERS) said on Wednesday it would use the Internet to recruit a firm to manage $1.2 billion of the system's domestic equity assets.
CalPERS said the selected firm would passively manage a portfolio that invests in small cap companies.

"Our use of the Internet for RFPs has proven to provide greater access for managers and the potential for the system to reach a large audience," Charles Valdes, chair of the CalPERS investment committee, said in a statement.
In April CalPERS posted its first request for proposal (RFP) on the Internet, seeking firms to manage more than $6 billion of the fund's domestic equity assets.
The system received 270 responses to the RFP over the Internet, triple the number of responses ever received by CalPERS in a single RFP.
CalPERS said it expected to complete both searches in March 1998.

CalPERS is the largest public pension fund in the United States with assets totaling more than $110 billion. The system administers retirement and health benefits to more than one million public employees.
The request for proposals were posted at: http://www.calpers.ca.gov/invest/rfp/index.html.
